rights_note: A secondary web reproduction with no rights statement (the Prairie library's ruling: 'unknown - link only'; the c. 1870 photograph is likely public domain by age, but its holder and the reproduction's terms are not established). Only forms, counts, places and proportions are read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset (no texture, no traced mesh), and the copy committed for the image gate (T-2755) is the store's, unaltered, with its attribution in the folder's README.

note: The only picture of 1637's south flank this project reads, and of the house before its remodel. It shows the south-west corner of a brick block two tall storeys over a raised basement under a deep dark cornice and a low hipped roof; on the front, a round-headed principal-storey light and a second-storey window over a band; the south wall blank brick back to an ornate stone-dressed projection, its front in tall round-arched lights between columns under a bracketed entablature, a balcony on its top before a shuttered round-headed window; a pale stone band along the wall's foot; a tall panelled stack over the eave; and a cast-iron fence of scrolled pickets across the foot. It is evidence of c. 1870, not of 1904: data/reference_views/spalding_house_1637_prairie/grosvenor_asbuilt_photo.match.json weighs each thing against the engraving and the 1911 sheet, and its camera's solve says how far its places can be read.
